title: Paragraphs and pace 1
summary: Whole paragraphs, read a few words ahead of your hands — the skill every drill so far was for.
intro: From here the course stops teaching keys and starts asking for pace. A paragraph is harder than a word list in one specific way: the words are not equally easy, so an even rhythm takes effort rather than luck. The trick is to keep your eyes two or three words ahead of your fingers, which feels wrong for about a minute and then feels like reading.
congrats: You have typed several paragraphs without looking down, which is what the whole course was for. One more lesson of this and then the final test — three minutes, one long passage, no new anything.

screens.content:
Touch typing is not a talent.
It is a habit, and habits take time rather than skill.
Ten minutes a day is enough.
screens.text: Short sentences to start. Read each line whole before you begin it, and let your hands follow your eyes rather than the other way round.
The words from that paragraph on their own. Notice which one your fingers hesitate over and remember it for the drill at the end of the unit.

screens.content:
For the first week you will be slower than you were before you started, and that is normal.
Your hands are learning where the keys are without your eyes to help them.
After that the speed arrives quickly, and it keeps arriving for months.
screens.text: Longer lines now. If you lose your place, keep going from where your eyes are rather than starting the line again.

screens.content:
The one rule that matters is not looking down.
Every glance at the keyboard teaches your hands to wait for your eyes.
Look at the screen, even while you are getting it wrong.
screens.text: This is the paragraph worth believing. Looking down feels like it helps and it is the single thing that keeps people at forty words a minute for twenty years.
A burst between two paragraphs, to reset the rhythm. Short words, no thinking required.

screens.content:
Accuracy comes before speed, and not by a little.
Someone typing 40 words a minute at 98 per cent will finish a page
long before someone typing 60 and fixing every third word.
screens.text: Numbers in the middle of prose, which is where they are most awkward. The hand has to leave the home row and come straight back.

screens.content:
Today I typed a whole paragraph without looking at my hands.
I did not think about a single key while I was doing it.
Next week I will be faster than I am now, and I will not notice it happening.
screens.text: Last screen, with Enter at the end of every line. Type it as though you meant it — in a few weeks it will be true.
